_comment: WHY THIS CHECK NEEDS ONE: its verdict reaches the owner through /cpp:status and
nothing downstream re-derives whether ~/.codex/AGENTS.md still carries
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md's rules. A blind version prints `current` over a Codex file
that has silently fallen behind - which is the state #1441 found on the host.
THE CASES ARE SANDBOXED HOMES: each case carries home/.claude/CLAUDE.md and
home/.codex/AGENTS.md. Both --home and --codex-home select the fixture, so
an inherited CODEX_HOME cannot redirect a case to the operator's real files (#1585).
THE GOOD CASE WAS BUILT BY THE GATE ITSELF (`--write` with both fixture roots). If the generated
format changes, rebuild it the same way: a stale good case reds this control,
which is the correct direction - it would otherwise certify a format nothing

cases.name: bad-source-gained-a-rule
cases.why: CLAUDE.md gained a Negative Control section after Codex's file was built. This is the measured #1441 defect: Codex never received that directive. Must read `stale`.

cases.name: bad-hand-edited
cases.why: A built Codex file with the old contradicting Nit Store sentence appended by hand. A rebuild would silently discard it, so it must read `hand-edited`, not `current`.

cases.name: good-fresh-pair
cases.why: A pair just built by --write. Separates a working check from one wedged on drift, which the bad cases alone cannot do.
